paper_metadata.title: Quantum Machine Learning Technique for Insurance Claim Fraud Detection with Quantum Feature Selection

experiments.description: Quantum support vector machine (QSVM) fraud-detection experiment on a home insurance claims dataset, using quantum feature selection and a ZZ feature map to classify transactions as fraudulent or non-fraudulent.

problem_formulation.encoding_details: Classical fraud features are mapped into a quantum feature map; the paper states a parametric quantum circuit U_phi(x) acting on n qubits and specifically uses a ZZ feature map with feature = 3.
problem_formulation.objective_function: Binary classification of insurance claims into fraudulent vs non-fraudulent using a kernel-based SVM decision boundary.

problem_instance.description: Home insurance claim fraud detection on real claims payment transactions with historical suspicious activity reporting (SAR) filings.

dataset_specification.description: Scrubbed insurance claims dataset with 15 weighted parameters, including credit score, payment default history, outstanding debts, property age, days unoccupied, claims history, loss timing flags, authority notification, and report availability. The paper does not report train/test split or exact sample count.

problem_instance.data_preprocessing_details: Normalize and scale the data; apply feature selection to reduce dimensionality; generate kernel function; implement the quantum circuit on a cloud-based quantum computer.
problem_instance.evaluation_methodology: Comparison of accuracy against classical KNN and SVM baselines; the paper reports accuracy values only and does not specify cross-validation or number of runs.

implementation_details.classical_preprocessing: Normalize and scale data; feature selection to reduce dimensions.
implementation_details.classical_postprocessing: Classify transactions using the QSVM decision function and compare accuracy with classical baselines.

speedup_claims.caveats: The paper reports comparable accuracy between classical and quantum methods, but no empirical or asymptotic speedup is demonstrated for this experiment.

complexity_analysis.quantum_complexity: O(log MN) is cited in the literature review for quantum SVM training/classification, but not derived for this experiment.
